a: A README explains what a project is, how to install it, and how to use it.
A changelog lists notable changes for each version of a project.
MIT License is a permissive open-source license allowing reuse with attribution.
Open source software shares source code so others can use, study, and improve it under a license.
Comment why, not what. Prefer clear names so code is self-explanatory.
Technical debt is the cost of quick shortcuts that make future changes harder.
Refactoring improves code structure without changing external behavior.
Pair programming is two developers working together on the same code.
Rubber duck debugging means explaining your code out loud to find bugs.
State the goal, what you tried, exact error messages, and a minimal example.
An RFC is a Request for Comments — a design proposal document for discussion.
An ADR (Architecture Decision Record) documents why a technical decision was made.
Use a short imperative summary (e.g. Fix login timeout) and optional body for details.
A linter statically analyzes code for bugs and style issues.
A formatter auto-rewrites code layout for consistent style.
A code smell is a sign the design may need cleanup (not necessarily a bug).
